ancestry_rule: FRANK/ClayCode agreement is not independent evidence. This lexical run is grounded primarily in ClayCode source/grammar self-conformance plus executable fuzzing and external parser architecture comparisons.

reviews.assumption: FRANK loop-of-loops requirements require a new FRANK-specific ClayCode syntax primitive.
reviews.origin_ancestry: FRANK plus prior ClayCode loop research
reviews.independent_check: Concurrent executable ClayCode loop runs represent tested recurrence with generic structured control and typed scheduler semantics; this run finds parser closure problems rather than a missing FRANK primitive.
reviews.counterhypothesis: A frozen H1 recurrence requirement will eventually expose an irreducible semantic gap in generic ClayCode control flow.
reviews.falsifier: Frozen H1 semantics cannot be parsed, represented or lowered without a FRANK-specific opaque escape after the generic parser/runtime is completed.

reviews.assumption: The current published ClayCode ref lexical rule is adequate as written.
reviews.independent_check: Executable 10000-case adjacent-ref probe demonstrates delimiter overconsumption under literal maximal munch; established parser designs independently make lexical boundaries/precedence explicit.
reviews.counterhypothesis: The real admitted parser already applies delimiter-aware contextual parsing, so only the EBNF text is stale.
reviews.falsifier: Locate and execute the canonical parser proving lossless delimiter-safe roundtrip with the current grammar contract unchanged.

reviews.assumption: Hyphen should simply be removed from bare identifiers.
reviews.independent_check: The repair removes the tested minus ambiguity but rejects all generated hyphenated names currently accepted. External language designs show split identifier/symbol classes are possible, but do not prove ClayCode's compatibility needs.
reviews.counterhypothesis: Contextual lexing or an explicit whitespace/operator rule preserves current bare names with lower migration cost.
reviews.falsifier: Repository-wide corpus and parser differential establish one candidate as semantically lossless with lower repair/migration cost.

reviews.assumption: Program semantic identity may be conflated with parser/compiler or execution provenance.
reviews.origin_ancestry: ClayCode identity research plus UnifiedDB/Harness constraints
reviews.independent_check: This run adds a pre-canonicalization discriminator: lexer policy changes interpretation before typed IR exists; concurrent transactional evidence separately requires execution/replay roots.
reviews.counterhypothesis: One monolithic source/contract hash is sufficient for semantic caching, provenance and replay.
reviews.falsifier: Matched equivalence and replay tests show no collision, false miss or unsafe reuse from the monolithic identity across formatting, parser versions, runtime schedules and transaction roots.
